guide.summary: A round grazer that eats shelled and shade-loving algae and Creambud, and eats dead material when it has no meal.
guide.biology: Real rotifers beat a crown of tiny hairs to sweep food into their mouths, and many also eat bits of dead matter.
guide.rules: Lives in water. Moves 0.8 cells per second and notices prey up to 4 cells away. Catches Glasswheel, Shadeleaf, Turnleaf and Creambud on contact, stores a meal of up to twice its own body, and waits 4 seconds before the next catch. Stops hunting when well fed. While it holds no meal it eats local detritus instead, using oxygen; a catch always comes first.
guide.example: Put Wheelgrazers in a dish with detritus but no algae and see how long the dead material keeps them going.
